cards.q: A loop of cord lies outside the introitus. What do you do with it?
options: Minimal handling; loose warm saline-soaked gauze
Push it back into the vagina
Wrap it tightly and pack with ice
Squeeze it to check the pulse
cards.why: Handling and cold cause cord spasm. Do not replace it.
cards.note: Some notes suggest replacing the cord into the vagina; RCOG advises against handling or replacing it.

cards.q: Cord prolapse in the ED. First hands-on action?
options: Manually elevate the presenting part off the cord and keep the hand in
cards.why: Lifting the presenting part relieves compression until delivery or until bladder filling takes over.

cards.q: Cord prolapse. Position while you wait in the bay?
cards.why: Knee–chest takes the most weight off the cord in the bay. For transfer: left lateral, head down, pillow under the left hip.

cards.q: Cord prolapse and theatre is 20 minutes away. Bladder filling volume?
options: 500–750 mL via a Foley, then clamp
cards.why: A full bladder lifts the presenting part. Empty it again before the caesarean.

cards.q: Cord prolapse, delivery delayed, the fetal heart stays abnormal after elevation. Tocolysis?
cards.why: Terbutaline reduces contractions that keep compressing the cord.

cards.q: Category 1 caesarean for cord prolapse. Decision-to-delivery standard?
cards.why: Category 1 is an immediate threat to life of mother or fetus; the audit standard is 30 minutes.

cards.q: Commonest cause of primary postpartum haemorrhage?
cards.why: The four Ts: tone, trauma, tissue, thrombin. Atony accounts for most.

cards.q: Primary PPH from atony. First-line uterotonic?
options: Oxytocin 5 IU by slow IV injection
cards.why: Oxytocin (or ergometrine if no hypertension) first, with uterine massage; then an infusion and second-line agents.

cards.q: PPH: tranexamic acid dose and timing?
options: 1 g IV as soon as possible, within 3 hours of birth
cards.why: WOMAN trial: 1 g IV early reduces death from bleeding; a second 1 g if bleeding continues.

options: 4 g IV over 5–15 min, then 1 g/h for 24 h
cards.why: Magnesium is the anticonvulsant of choice; a further 2–4 g if seizures recur.

cards.q: Magnesium toxicity: loss of reflexes and slow breathing. Antidote?
cards.why: Stop the infusion and give calcium gluconate.
McRoberts with suprapubic pressure resolves many cases. Fundal pressure is contraindicated.
